articles.title: Why GTA 6 actors may stay silent until release day despite growing cast speculation
articles.summary: Esports News: Grand Theft Auto 6 fans may have to wait until the game launches to learn who is behind its biggest characters. Rockstar Games has reportedly reminded.
articles.body: Grand Theft Auto 6 fans may have to wait until the game launches to learn who is behind its biggest characters. Rockstar Games has reportedly reminded actors who worked on GTA 6 that their non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) remain active until the game’s release on November 19. The reported warning comes as fans continue to guess the game’s cast from resumes, voice clips, and small hints. Rockstar has not officially confirmed the reported email, but the message could explain why many actors have stayed quiet about their roles.GTA 6 actors reportedly told to stay silent until November 19According to a report shared by GTA VI O’Clock, Rockstar reportedly sent an email reminding people who worked on the game about their NDAs. The message allegedly said that the date when they can announce their involvement is still November 19.The report claims the warning may have been sent to everyone who worked on GTA 6 in a performance role. This could include actors involved in voice acting, motion capture, or other performance work, rather than only the main stars.The reported email comes after actor Stephen Root became the first known GTA 6 actor to publicly confirm his role. Root told the Associated Press that he plays Brian Heder in the game.Root also explained why he believed his role became known. He said that too many people already knew him from King of the Hill and could recognize his voice. His comments gave fans one of their first clear pieces of information about the GTA 6 cast.Rockstar reportedly keeps GTA 6 cast mystery aliveRockstar has always kept GTA 6 details very secret. So far, fans have had to work out the possible cast using actor resumes, voice comparisons, and other clues instead of official announcements.The reported NDA reminder could mean fans will not get a big cast reveal before launch. Rockstar may also avoid introducing its actors through trailers, magazines, or other official promotions before November 19.Two names that continue to appear in fan discussions are Manni L. Perez and Dylan Rourke. Perez has been widely linked to Lucia, while Rourke has been connected to Jason. However, neither casting has been officially confirmed by Rockstar, and Perez has previously denied being involved.For now, Rockstar has not publicly commented on the reported email. That means the full cast remains a mystery.If the reported NDA reminder is real, GTA 6 actors may have to keep their roles secret until the game arrives on November 19. Stephen Root’s confirmation has already given fans one confirmed name, but Rockstar still appears to be keeping the rest of the cast hidden. articles.title: Driver charged over fatal A61 Barnsley crash that killed six people
articles.summary: Four members of the same family and a married couple on a motorbike died in the 2024 collision.
articles.body:
A man has been charged with causing death by dangerous driving over a crash that killed six people, including two children.

Shannen Morgan and Shane Roller died along with two of their daughters, nine-year-old Rubie, and Lillie, four, when the family's car collided with a motorbike on the A61 between Barnsley and Wakefield on 21 July 2024.

Husband and wife Christopher and Janine Barton, from Barnsley, who were both travelling on the motorcycle, also died in the crash.

Christopher Cockell, 50, is due to appear at Leeds Magistrates' Court in October charged with six counts of causing death by dangerous driving.

An inquest previously heard that the silver Ford Focus being driven by Mr Roller, 33, collided head on with the BMW motorcycle being driven by Mr Barton, 56, at about 15:50 BST between Staincross and Newmillerdam.

Wakefield Coroner's Court heard the collision happened as the motorcycle was overtaking another vehicle on the single-carriageway road, which had a 50mph (80 km/h) speed limit.

Coroner's support officer Phil Marr told the hearing: "As a result of a head-on impact, the car was spun to the side of the road, where it caught fire.

"It was not possible to release any of the occupants and all four were pronounced dead by paramedics at the scene."

Marr said a pathologist concluded Mr Barton's provisional cause of death was due to head and chest injuries.

He said Mrs Barton was "thrown onto the adjacent golf course" in the collision, with her death due to chest injuries.

Ms Morgan and van driver Mr Roller, who lived in Athersley, Barnsley, had another daughter, aged 11, who was not with them at the time of the crash.

An online fundraising page, set up by a family friend in the wake of the tragedy, raised more than £400,000 for her.

In a social media post at the time, Mr Roller's father, Graham, paid tribute to the couple, who he described as an "amazing" mum and dad.

"Shane wasn't just a son but an amazing father and he had a heart of gold," he wrote.

"Shannen, our daughter-in-law, was funny and was also an amazing mum and they thought the world of their little family."

Co-head teachers of Athersley North Primary School, which Rubie and Lillie had attended, said the girls had been "a delight to teach".

In a statement, Clare Storr and Kirsty Wordsworth, said: "The girls were a credit to their parents, who were always incredibly supportive and who will also be greatly missed."

Mr and Mrs Barton, 48, who had lived in Barnsley, had recently celebrated their 25th wedding anniversary.

In a tribute issued via West Yorkshire Police in 2024, their son described his parents as "a loving, caring mum and dad who always put me before everything else".

A spokesperson for West Yorkshire Police said Cockell had been summoned following an investigation by the force's Major Collision Enquiry Team and would appear before magistrates on 28 October.

Cockell, of Gresford Close, Woolley Grange, had already been facing a charge of failing to stop at the scene of a collision.

articles.title: 49ers face logjam on injured reserve with Demarcus Robinson out 3-6 weeks
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers WR Demarcus Robinson and DT James Thompson Jr. have high ankle sprains that could cost them a month and a half, but the crowd of players...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers look like a legitimate contender through two weeks. At the same time, the team already has so many injuries that it is considering keeping players with multi-week ailments on the active roster, rather than placing them on the injured reserve list.

NFL teams can place an unlimited number of players on IR during a given season. Players must miss a minimum of four games once put on IR. But only eight of them can be designated to return. Thus, as wide receiver Demarcus Robinson and defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. grapple with high ankle sprains that could keep them on the shelf for 3-6 weeks, according to head coach Kyle Shanahan, the 49ers may hold both players on the active roster so as to not cut into those eight spots.

"Those guys (Robinson and Thompson) are right in that area … of how long those take (to recover from)," Shanahan said. "(But) it's real early for us to have as many (injuries) as we've had, so we got to balance all that out."

Robinson caught three passes for 34 yards before he was carted to the locker room early in the 49ers' 35-13 shellacking of the Miami Dolphins on Sunday at Levi's Stadium. Robinson had worked his way into the No. 3 receiver role for San Francisco following injuries to Ricky Pearsall and De'Zhaun Stribling .

"Yeah, it sucks," quarterback Brock Purdy said postgame of Robinson's injury. "These are all extremely great playmakers that, looking at our roster in OTAs and camp, it's like, 'Oh shoot, we can do some damage.' And then Ricky goes down, Stribling, and now D-Rob. … for them to go down early in the season like that is tough."

In the meantime, Shanahan said fellow wide receivers Jacob Cowing , Jordan Watkins and KhaDarel Hodge will have increased roles, while the 49ers' front office is "working on all possibilities, looking at everything that's out there" for possible outside reinforcements.

Also worth noting: Shanahan said the 49ers will have to manage the workload of wide receiver Mike Evans - who left Sunday's game with a hip injury - throughout practices this week. But it doesn't sound like his hip is a major concern at the moment.

As for the defensive line, Thompson's injury further damages the 49ers' interior depth, as it follows the season-ending injury to second-year defensive tackle Alfred Collins . Thompson, an undrafted rookie, rotated in for 19 snaps Sunday prior to getting hurt. The healthy defensive tackles on the 49ers' active roster are Osa Odighizuwa , Gracen Halton and CJ West. Halton, another rookie, had a standout performance Sunday and has already earned an increased role in defensive coordinator Raheem Morris' system.

San Francisco has the following players on IR who could be designated to return at some point: Stribling, WR Christian Kirk , OL Austen Pleasants, CB Nate Hobbs , LB Nick Martin and DL Sam Okuayinonu . It's unlikely all those players will be back on the active roster this year, but the first three are the most obvious candidates. Kirk is eligible to return to practice after the 49ers' Oct. 4 matchup against the Denver Broncos .
